function.description:
Returns field notice network devices. Use this tool for questions such as 'What devices have field notices?', 'Show devices scanned for field notices.', 'Give devices with more than N notices.', 'List devices with noticeCount greater than N.', or follow-up questions asking which devices the confirmed field notices pertain to. Use this list API, not the count API, whenever the user asks to give, list, show, display, or enumerate devices, even if a noticeCount threshold is provided. An answer that includes raw device id values is invalid. Do not claim NOT_SCANNED devices have field notices. Each row in the final table MUST include only device name, management IP, and number of confirmed field notices (noticeCount). Do not include potentialNoticeCount or potential field notices unless the user explicitly asks for potential field notices.

MANDATORY POST-PROCESSING: The returned networkDeviceId is an internal device UUID for backend lookup only. For every device row that will be included in the final answer, call get_device_details with device_id set to that exact networkDeviceId value. A get_device_details call without device_id is invalid for this workflow because it returns an unrelated generic device list. Never join field-notice rows to device details by row order, offset, time range, or first returned device. If get_device_details does not return a matching device whose id equals the field-notice networkDeviceId, do not include that row in the main device table and do not infer or fabricate the device name or management IP. Instead, mention separately that some devices could not be enriched.
function.name: api_getFieldNoticeNetworkDevices

limit.description: Maximum number of records to be fetched. If not provided, 500 records will be fetched by default

noticeCount.description: Return network devices with confirmed noticeCount greater than this noticeCount.

offset.description: The first record to show for this page. Minimum value is 1

order.description: Whether ascending or descending order should be used to sort the response. Available values : asc, desc. Default value is asc.

scanStatus.description: Status of the scan on the network device. Available values : NOT_SCANNED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILED.

sortBy.description: A property within the response to sort by.

comments.description: More details about the scan status. ie:- if the scan status is failed, comments will give the reason for failure

lastScanTime.description: Time at which the device was scanned

networkDeviceId.description: Internal device UUID for backend lookup only. Do not present this raw value in user-facing output. Use get_device_details with device_id set to this exact UUID to resolve device name and management IP.

noticeCount.description: Number of confirmed field notices to which the network device is vulnerable.

potentialNoticeCount.description: Number of potential field notices to which the network device may be vulnerable. Do not include this value in final answers unless the user explicitly asks for potential field notices.

scanStatus.description: 'NOT_SCANNED' - the device was not scanned. 'IN_PROGRESS' - a scan is in progress for the device. 'SUCCESS' - device scan was successful. 'FAILED' - device scan failed
